inference: Sparse backing removes the previous /dev/shm capacity objection: stock QEMU can expose the 8G BAR without physically allocating 8G first.
The current nested platform can prove the ESXi large-MMIO mapping gate at 8G, but cannot complete an EFI Linux boot with that BAR.
This is not evidence that bare-metal ESXi rejects an 8G BAR. It is a nested execution/firmware observability boundary, so 32G and 64G were not run blindly on the same platform.
A power-on-only probe or a custom endpoint that does not force full guest enumeration is the next safe way to test the greater-than-32G SizeGB threshold.
